answer: The strongest lever is simple: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because anchor only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, basalt is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any ocean approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
